secondary_audit_views.content: Frozen head contains executable implementation, training/evaluation/test/result/plot plumbing but no persisted execution record. Implementation presence therefore carries no execution/result standing.

Agency-transfer docs/config/main disagree on episode/phasing detail; permeability protocol constrains kappa to [0,1], config/main extend to 2.0, config step .05/100 trials while main uses .1/no trial loop, and main plots deterministic kappa/(1+kappa) rather than the documented changing-environment experiment.

Pytest source exists, but frozen head has no associated GitHub Actions runs or combined status records. test source != test execution != pass. tests/test_agents.py also attempts abstract BaseAgent construction under ordinary ABC semantics, but no frozen run artifact establishes an observed failure.
Experiment logger/results/serialization/visualization code can create artifacts if run; the 81-path frozen head contains no results directory, run manifest, persisted metric file, or plot image.

Frozen source exposes package export name mismatch in environments; registry names/import expectations diverge from current helper modules; EvaluationLoop calls act_without_assistance absent from parsed agents; AncestorTrainer calls generic update while current agent subclasses inherit no-op model update; these are implementation/integration defects, not scientific negative results.

Agency/dependency/permeability/diversity/sovereignty metrics and reward code implement arithmetic proxies. TransferTaskEnv awards 1.0 for independent_reasoning=True and agency helper supplies that flag; permeability helper counts error-triggered update calls although BaseAgent update_model may be no-op. Objective/proxy implementation does not establish construct validity.
Two different ExperimentLogger classes exist under src/experiments/logger.py and src/utils/logger.py with filesystem versus in-memory semantics. Same class name does not establish object identity.
Citations and related-framework comparisons are conceptual context. They do not create endpoint identity, dependency, support, authority transfer or Program Map edges to external frameworks.
